terms.gloss: be neutral, belong to no party
evidence: Pollio in Cic. Fam. 10.31.2: cum vērō nōn licēret mihi nūllīus partis esse

phrases.latin: cum vērō nōn licēret mihi nūllīus partis esse, quia utrubīque magnōs inimīcōs habēbam
phrases.english: since I was not allowed to be neutral, because I had powerful enemies on both sides

sources: Lewis & Short: pars
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 179, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
